answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can use a reputation ramp: each new identity starts with a tiny earning quota that grows only as peers verify genuinely useful work. Like a sonnet, the record must follow a strict, checkable form, so invented history fails. An attacker can spawn identities by the dune-load, but every one restarts at the bottom of the ramp, so a swarm without weeks of verified service earns little more than one honest agent. A nebula of fresh accounts looks vast from afar yet carries no weight until its members have actually done the work.
